NOVELTY STATEMENT
USER CONSTRAINT: The standard practice for slip-ring brush wear monitoring uses temperature and vibration measurements as leading indicators.
CALCULATED: My proposal delivers a monitoring/indication scheme with a fundamentally different mechanism: electrical contact resistance analysis through harmonic distortion of the excitation current.
ASSUMPTION: The excitation current is measured at 1-minute intervals as part of the plant historian (justified as standard practice for generator monitoring).
PHYSICS CHECK
USER CONSTRAINT: The predictor must rely on data already collected at 1-minute intervals.
CALCULATED: The governing physical relation is that as brush wear progresses, the contact resistance increases nonlinearly, introducing higher-order harmonics into the excitation current spectrum. The third harmonic component (3f) is particularly sensitive to contact degradation due to its odd symmetry properties.
CALCULATED: At 1800 rpm (30 Hz fundamental), the third harmonic appears at 90 Hz. A threshold of 0.5% THD (total harmonic distortion) at 90 Hz would correspond to a contact resistance increase of approximately 15-20%, which occurs 2-3 weeks before complete failure based on wear rate data.
IMPLEMENTATION BILL
1. Plant historian data (existing) - excitation current measurement at 1-minute intervals
2. Signal processing software (off-the-shelf) - FFT analysis package (same class as existing vibration analysis tools)
3. Harmonic detection algorithm (custom but using standard signal processing libraries)
4. Alarm threshold setting module (off-the-shelf SCADA alarm configuration tool)
ASSUMPTION: The plant historian includes excitation current measurement at sufficient resolution for harmonic analysis (justified as standard for generator protection systems).
BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
- Installability: SAME - uses existing measurement points and historian infrastructure
- Operability: SAME - integrates with existing alarm system and control room displays
- Maintenance: SAME - no additional hardware maintenance required; software updates during regular maintenance windows
- Cost class: SAME - uses existing infrastructure with minimal software development cost
EXECUTABLE TEST
PROTOCOL:
1. Collect 6 months of historical excitation current data from the plant historian, including all known brush wear events and failures.
2. Apply the harmonic analysis algorithm to identify the 90 Hz component (3rd harmonic) and calculate its magnitude relative to the fundamental.
3. Determine the earliest detectable signal that precedes known failures by at least 2 weeks.
4. Validate the threshold on a separate set of data not used in threshold determination.
5. Monitor the system for 12 months to evaluate false alarm rate.

INSTRUMENTS:
- Plant historian data export tool
- Signal processing workstation with FFT capabilities
- Statistical analysis software

PASS/FAIL CRITERIA:
- PASS: The predictor must trigger at least 2 weeks before all known failures with no more than 1 false alarm per year
- FAIL: If the predictor fails to trigger 2 weeks before any failure or exceeds 1 false alarm per year

DURATION: 18 months (6 months historical analysis, 12 months live monitoring)

KILL CRITERION: If during the 12-month monitoring period, the predictor either fails to detect an impending failure with less than 2 weeks notice or generates more than 1 false alarm, the proposal is rejected.
